name: PBB Hotline
shortDescription: Local emergency intake, incident handling, command reporting, and support coordination for barangay and command nodes.
longDescription: PBB Hotline / Vox is the local emergency operations surface for citizens, operators, command users, and administrators. It supports emergency intake, incident work, team assignment, command alerts, SITREP preparation, and support requests from a PBB node.

The module uses local node services for live communication and maps. Its confirmed upstream paths are selective: completed SITREP and support-request workflows can be handed to Relay, while editable incident records are not broadly replicated between nodes.

readiness.note: Core citizen, operator, command, SITREP, support-request, Realtime, and MapServer workflows are implemented and integrated.
remainingWork: Define production retention and media-handling policy.
Complete deployment runbooks and security hardening.
Document browser behavior during complete local network loss.

problemSolved: During an emergency, reports can arrive through fragmented calls and messages while operators lack a shared local view. Vox provides one node-local workflow for intake, incident handling, command reporting, and requests for outside support.

workflowSteps.title: Report locally
workflowSteps.description: A citizen reaches the local Hotline surface and starts an emergency report while connected to the node network.

workflowSteps.title: Triage and coordinate
workflowSteps.description: Operators review incident details, location, resources, team assignments, messages, and media in the local workbench.

workflowSteps.title: Build command context
workflowSteps.description: Command staff issue alerts and prepare structured situation reports from local operational information.

workflowSteps.title: Send selected updates
workflowSteps.description: SITREPs and support requests can enter Relay-backed delivery and retry workflows when the route upstream is available.

localCapabilities: Citizen intake, operator incident work, command reporting, messages, and local media storage can continue over the node LAN while the app and database are available.
SITREP and support-request delivery records can persist locally for server-side retry.
requiresLocalServices: PBB Realtime is required for supported live presence, call, message, and media events.
PBB MapServer must be prepared and available for offline tiles and boundaries.
syncsWhenConnected: The latest SITREP can be handed to PBB Relay through a persisted delivery path.
Support requests and their confirmed lifecycle updates can move through Relay and PBB Support System.
connectivityRequired: Delivery to an upstream or peer node waits for a reachable Relay route.
Map cache misses may require an upstream tile provider if the requested area was not prepared.
notSynchronized: No durable browser-side citizen report outbox is confirmed.
Editable incident records are not broadly synchronized between nodes.

faqs.question: Can Hotline keep working when the internet is down?
faqs.answer: Yes, local work can continue while Hotline and its supporting services are running on the local PBB network. Messages meant for another node will wait until a connection becomes available.

faqs.question: Can a citizen submit a report after leaving the local network?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. The current design does not confirm that a browser can save a report while disconnected and send it later. Hotline's offline support applies within the local PBB network.

faqs.question: Are live incident records copied to every PBB node?
faqs.answer: No. Full editable incident records are not copied everywhere. Nodes send only selected situation reports and support-request updates through Relay.

faqs.question: What does PBB Realtime provide to Vox?
faqs.answer: PBB Realtime supports live updates for who is connected, calls, messages, media, and other app activity. One shared Realtime service is expected to run on each node.

faqs.question: Will maps always be available offline?
faqs.answer: No. Only map areas and boundaries prepared in advance will work reliably offline. Looking outside those prepared areas may require internet access.

faqs.question: How does Vox ask another operations team for support?
faqs.answer: Vox saves the request locally, then Relay can send the approved request details to a designated PBB Support node. That node can return updates as the request is handled.
